q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of frozen parathas per kg?
title: Frozen paratha carbon footprint per kg
short: Weigh the flour, fat and fillings per kg and use supplier figures. Add dough making, pressing, par cooking fuel, blast freezing and cold storage electricity and packing, then divide plant energy by kg packed. Freezing is often a large energy share.

ul: Wheat flour, ghee, oil or margarine.
Par cooking on gas or electric griddles.
Spiral or blast freezers and cold storage.

p: Report per kg packed. If the buyer asks for frozen storage to the port, add it as a separate line.

example.title: Worked example: frozen paratha plant per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 68,720 / 150,000 = 0.458 kg CO2 per kg
Add flour, fat, fillings and packaging for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
